submissions.findingTextShort: A 29-day Cognitaven green-oat extract trial reported selected cognition and physiological stress-response signals but no mood effect.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A randomized double-blind placebo-controlled dose-ranging trial assigned 132 healthy adults aged 35–65 to Cognitaven green-oat extract at 430, 860 or 1290 mg/day or placebo for 29 days. Selected working-memory/multitasking measures improved at some doses and the highest chronic dose reduced electrodermal response to a laboratory stressor, while no treatment-related mood effect was detected. These are proprietary green-oat-extract findings rather than evidence for generic oatstraw or milky-oat tincture.
submissions.populationContext: Healthy adults aged 35–65 in a 29-day dose-ranging trial.
submissions.usageContext: Cognitaven proprietary green-oat extract, 430/860/1290 mg/day; not milky oat tops tincture.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Dose-specific/selective outcomes and commercial product identity constrain generalization. Draft-only pending governance.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 12-week Neuravena wild-green-oat crossover trial found no sustained cognitive benefit in older adults with normal cognition.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A randomized double-blind placebo-controlled crossover trial in 37 healthy older adults tested Neuravena wild-green-oat extract at 1500 mg/day for 12 weeks. Chronic supplementation did not improve any measured cognitive outcome. This null long-duration result must coexist with shorter acute/29-day signals and prevents a simple `long-term cognitive benefit` claim.
submissions.populationContext: Healthy older adults with normal cognition.
submissions.usageContext: Neuravena wild-green-oat extract, 1500 mg/day for 12 weeks.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Small sample limits power, but the direct chronic null result remains first-class. Draft-only pending source governance.

submissions.findingTextShort: An acute Neuravena crossover study reported a selected processing-speed signal at 800 mg in middle-aged adults with subjective memory decline.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A double-blind placebo-controlled counterbalanced crossover study in healthy adults aged 40–65 who reported age-related memory decline tested single doses of wild green-oat extract. The 800 mg condition improved speed on a global timed-task measure across post-dose assessments. This acute selective signal should remain separate from chronic outcomes and cannot be transferred to whole oatstraw or tincture preparations.
submissions.populationContext: Middle-aged healthy adults with subjective memory decline.
submissions.usageContext: Single-dose Neuravena wild-green-oat extract; selected acute cognition context.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Acute selective-task findings do not establish durable cognitive or stress benefit. Draft-only pending governance.

submissions.findingTextShort: A six-RCT systematic review found more favorable acute/short-term than long-term green-oat cognition evidence and rated the evidence only average quality.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A systematic review of six randomized controlled trials involving 287 healthy participants concluded that acute Avena sativa extract supplementation may improve selected cognitive accuracy/speed outcomes, short-term chronic supplementation showed some favorable findings, and long-term chronic supplementation did not. Doses and formulations varied and overall evidence quality was average, so the literature supports an acute-versus-chronic evidence split rather than a stable generic cognitive benefit.
submissions.populationContext: Healthy adults across six randomized oat-extract trials.
submissions.usageContext: Avena sativa green/wild oat extracts with heterogeneous doses; not equivalent to whole straw or milky-oat tincture.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Small trial count, dose disparity and formulation heterogeneity limit confidence. Draft-only pending governance.

submissions.findingTextShort: The current milky-oat-tops tincture dose text and broad sedative/antidepressant/pregnancy cautions are not established by the located green-oat-extract trials.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: The live Oatstraw profile refers to `Milky oat tops tincture` in dosage text and carries broad cautions about sedatives, alcohol, sleep aids, antidepressants and pregnancy/breastfeeding. The located human trials test standardized green/wild oat extracts and do not validate a tincture regimen or quantify those interaction/reproductive risks. Separate preparation-specific efficacy and safety receipts are required before those propositions can be promoted.
submissions.usageContext: Preparation and safety provenance gap; no consumer dose or interaction recommendation is generated here.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Missing receipt does not prove a risk is absent; it requires independent validation. Keep NEEDS_REVIEW/noindex.
